newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa stays lower by close, rangebound.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa stays lower by close, rangebound.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ended lower on Tuesday, but remained range-bound after listless trade marked by light origin selling and trade buying, traders said.

Price movements were kept within a narrow five stg range on a lack of affirmative fundamental news, pushing the market into what appears to be a prolonged slumber. "The market is disinterested, maintaining a generalised trading range," said one trader.

"There doesn't seem to be much fundamentally out there to really get the market going, so it's just maintaining itself." By the close, most-active December was five stg lower at 984 stg a tonne, after gapping three stg lower at the open.
The contract has been trapped in the 980-990 stg band for the past week.

Overall volume reached a total 2,323 lots after a sleepy morning session which saw a mere 380 lots changing hands. Fundamentally, cocoa analysts said they expect the UK third quarter cocoa grind to rise by about 10 percent to 38,000 tonnes from 34,400 in the same quarter in 1995.
The increase would reflect resumed production at one of the Mars grinding plants and the general upturn in cocoa consumption in the country.
The UK grind data is not due until the second week of October.

Technical analysts said cocoa looked fragile on the charts and could face an uphill task clearing the closely-watched 1,000 stg barrier, basis December. The December contract last tested the 1,000-mark on September 16.
